source_references.title: Southwest uses AI to modernize management software: PwC

business_problem: Southwest Airlines needed to modernize a legacy crew attendance and leave system whose undocumented logic and aging stack made maintenance, planning, and future change slow and risky.
solution_summary: Southwest Airlines used generative AI as the core engine for modernizing a legacy crew leave and attendance application before any rewrite work began. PwC built a Microsoft Azure-based approach that reverse-engineered complex source code into functional requirements and a prioritized modernization backlog. GenAI capabilities automated code analysis, dependency mapping, and user-story generation, while Southwest’s knowledge specialists and PwC teams iteratively reviewed outputs in workshops to align them with operational needs. Instead of spending months reconstructing undocumented business logic by hand, the teams condensed planning and design into a five-week milestone with a high-confidence delivery plan. The resulting backlog covered more than 600 high-quality user stories and created a repeatable method for translating legacy applications into actionable modernization programs that save engineering time, reduce risk, and accelerate future development.

data_flow: Legacy crew-management source code flows through PwC’s Azure-based GenAI pipeline, which extracts requirements, maps dependencies, and generates user stories. Southwest specialists then review and refine the outputs in workshops, turning undocumented application logic into a prioritized backlog and delivery plan for the modernization program.

business_outcome: Southwest halved backlog-creation time, created a high-confidence modernization plan with more than 600 accepted user stories, and established a faster, more accurate way to prepare legacy systems for redevelopment.

evidence_quotes: GenAI capabilities were used to pull unique insights and requirements directly from the source code, reducing project planning time by half.
PwC brought an innovative engineering approach along with GenAI, built on Microsoft Azure, to reverse-engineer the legacy system’s complex source code into holistic functional requirements.

While GenAI tools automated labor-intensive tasks like scalable code analysis and dependency mapping, PwC facilitated workshops and iterative reviews that helped align the outputs with our operational needs — blending leading-edge technology with strategic human insights.
